fieldData.course-description: Learners explore theory, research, and application of research within the scientific study of human personality.
fieldData.extendededcoursedesc: Learners explore theory, research, and application of research within the scientific study of human personality. They examine foundational concepts and major theoretical approaches to the study of personality. Learners apply dominant theoretical perspectives to the real world while also considering life stage, gender, culture, the workplace, relationships, and personality disorders.
fieldData.name: Personality

fieldData.course-description: This course offers an interdisciplinary exploration of Canada’s health care system, with a focus on health and wellness across diverse populations.
fieldData.extendededcoursedesc: This course offers an interdisciplinary exploration of Canada’s health care system, with a focus on health and wellness across diverse populations. Learners will examine the roles of helping professionals—especially those in community and human services—in promoting well-being, navigating health systems, and advocating for equitable access to care. Students will analyze current health issues, explore the social determinants of health, and consider their own role in health and wellness promotion. A core emphasis will be placed on understanding health misinformation, wellness strategies, and the intersection of physical, emotional, and social health.
fieldData.name: Health, Wellness, and Professional Practice in Canada’s Health Care System

fieldData.course-description: Explore how individuals, businesses, and governments make choices when resources are scarce, and how markets and other institutions determine what gets produced, how it is produced, and who gets it.
fieldData.extendededcoursedesc: Explore how individuals, businesses, and governments make choices when resources are scarce, and how markets and other institutions determine what gets produced, how it is produced, and who gets it. Develop core economic tools like opportunity cost, supply and demand, and market equilibrium to make sense of real-world issues such as prices, wages, housing, and market power. Examine consumer behaviour and how firms organize production under different market structures, and how to apply microeconomic thinking to topics like international trade, marginal decision-making, and the trade-off between efficiency and equity.  The goal of this course is to become better equipped to analyze everyday economic questions and make more informed personal, business, and policy decisions.
fieldData.name: Principles of Microeconomics

fieldData.course-description: Explore how organizations design compensation, benefits, and rewards that truly motivate people. In this course, you’ll connect strategy to pay, evaluate jobs, and examine real compensation practices and legislation in Canada and Alberta.
fieldData.extendededcoursedesc: This course focuses on the total rewards package, including compensation, benefits, and monetary and non-monetary rewards. It emphasizes the importance of aligning organizational strategy with the total rewards approach as a foundation for this human resource functional area. Students gain practical experience in job evaluation, linking performance standards to compensation plans, and researching Canada and Alberta legislative acts as well as compensation trends.
fieldData.name: Compensation & Benefits

fieldData.course-description: Learn how to design and deliver training that truly engages employees and supports growth. This course blends adult learning principles with hands-on program design and facilitation skills to help create impactful learning experiences.
fieldData.extendededcoursedesc: This course takes a dynamic, hands-on approach to designing training programs that support employee learning and development. Students explore key adult learning principles, core elements of program planning, and facilitation strategies that create meaningful and engaging learning experiences. Through practical application, students develop skills to design training programs that support professional growth and organizational success.
fieldData.name: Employee Learning and Development

fieldData.course-description: Discover how HR professionals guide organizations through change from start to finish. This course explores real-world change management strategies, current trends, and how to support successful, lasting transformation.
fieldData.extendededcoursedesc: This course examines the role of human resource professionals within the context of change management theories. Students analyze and apply change management theories and strategies to a variety of business scenarios. The focus is on the full change process, from initiation through to sustaining change. Current trends in change management are also identified and discussed.
fieldData.name: Change Management

fieldData.course-description: Step into the veterinary field and learn how clinics operate from the inside out. This course explores veterinary team roles, ethics, safety, animal welfare, and how clinics build trust and reputation in their communities.
fieldData.extendededcoursedesc:
This course introduces students to the veterinary industry and profession by exploring roles within a veterinary team, relevant legislation, and the ethical standards required in practice. It covers essential workplace policies, including safety protocols, risk recognition, and measures to protect staff, animals, and visitors. Students also examine how to recognize and respond to animal cruelty and abuse, supporting their ethical responsibility to animal welfare. In addition, the course explores marketing strategies for veterinary clinics and the role staff play in building a positive clinic reputation.

‍
fieldData.name: Introduction to the Veterinary Profession

fieldData.course-description: Build a strong foundation in personal financial planning and learn how financial decisions shape long-term well-being. This course also supports the CFP Core Curriculum pathway and pairs well with Financial Markets and Products.
fieldData.extendededcoursedesc: This course introduces fundamental financial planning knowledge and the personal financial planning process. Students explore key concepts that influence an individual’s and family’s financial well-being. The course also focuses on collecting and analyzing essential information to begin the financial planning process. It is eligible toward the Certified Financial Planner (CFP) Core Curriculum program. It is recommended that students enroll in Financial Markets and Products (FNSR2301) in the same term.
fieldData.name: Personal Financial Planning I

fieldData.course-description: Explore how money, banking, and Canada’s financial system work together in real-world practice. This course builds the foundation for financial planning and supports the CFP Core Curriculum pathway.
fieldData.extendededcoursedesc: This course introduces the concept of money, the Canadian financial industry, and the impact of the regulatory environment. Students analyze financial products and services available to customers, including the adjudication of credit. These concepts form the foundation of the financial planning process. This course is eligible toward the Financial Planning Certificate of Achievement program.
fieldData.name: Financial Markets & Products

fieldData.course-description: Learn how data shapes better business decisions. This course introduces analytics tools like Excel, SQL, and Power BI while building skills in data visualization and real-world analysis.
fieldData.extendededcoursedesc: This course introduces business analytics as a method for improving business decision-making. Students explore descriptive, predictive, and prescriptive analytics, with opportunities to compile and work with database analytics, including querying databases. The focus is on descriptive analytics to create data visualizations for real-world applications. Students also use Excel and are introduced to tools such as SQL and Power BI.
fieldData.name: Introduction to Business Analytics

fieldData.course-description: Strengthen your drawing skills by learning how to see and build form with confidence. This course explores line, light, perspective, and composition to help you bring ideas to life visually.
fieldData.extendededcoursedesc: This course provides an in-depth study of drawing principles essential for observation and developing visual ideas. Students analyze line, form, and lighting to communicate concepts through believable imagery. Key topics also include perspective, composition, and value patterns.
fieldData.name: Sketching for Communication

fieldData.course-description: Build a deeper understanding of Autism Spectrum Disorder and its impact across the lifespan. This course develops practical knowledge to help you support individuals and families with care and confidence.
fieldData.extendededcoursedesc: Autism Spectrum Disorder (ASD) is a lifelong condition that impacts a person’s development throughout the lifespan. This introductory course explores ASD, its characteristics, and its impact on individuals and families over time. Students gain knowledge and skills to support individuals and families experiencing ASD.
fieldData.name: Introduction to Autism Spectrum Disorder

fieldData.course-description: Learn how case managers bring people and services together to support effective care. This course explores collaboration, coordination, and advocacy across health and human services settings.
fieldData.extendededcoursedesc: Case managers advocate for, design, and support high-quality client care within the health and human services sectors. They collaborate with professionals, individuals, families, and communities to plan and coordinate care. This course examines diverse professional perspectives and the responsibilities involved in integrating, coordinating, and collaborating services.
fieldData.name: Case Management

fieldData.course-description: Explore how policy shapes health and human services and the systems behind it. This course looks at how policies are created, influenced, and changed—and the role managers play in that process.
fieldData.extendededcoursedesc: Policy creates the structure for delivering health and human services. Through the lens of the social determinants of health, students examine the origins and development of policy and how it is influenced by politics, interest groups, and advocacy. Students also explore how health and human service managers work with policy and contribute to policy change.
fieldData.name: Social Determinants of Health

fieldData.course-description: Discover how technology is reshaping health and human services. This course explores real-world opportunities, challenges, and ethical considerations while building strategies for leading technology-driven change.
fieldData.extendededcoursedesc: Current and emerging technologies create a wide range of possibilities in health and human services. This course examines the opportunities and barriers of evolving technologies in these sectors. Through the perspective of a health and human services manager, students explore the impact of increasing reliance on technology by individuals, organizations, and society. Students also develop strategies for implementing technology-enabled change initiatives while addressing related ethics and privacy considerations.
fieldData.name: Digital Transformations in Health and Human Services

fieldData.course-description: Learn how impactful health and human service programs are built from the ground up. This course develops skills in needs analysis, program design, evaluation, and data-informed decision-making.
fieldData.extendededcoursedesc: This course focuses on the skills needed to develop effective programs in health and human services. Students examine the processes and methods of program design and evaluation, including program design principles, understanding social problems, and conducting needs analysis. The course also covers selecting appropriate intervention strategies, setting goals and objectives, designing effective programs, and collecting and analyzing program data.
fieldData.name: Program Design and Evaluation

fieldData.course-description: Explore how inclusive employment support helps people build meaningful roles at work and in the community. This course focuses on practical approaches that support individuals with disabilities in reaching their potential.
fieldData.extendededcoursedesc: This course introduces historical and current models of employment supports for individuals facing barriers to employment. Students explore practices that support individuals in discovering personal and professional potential through work and community participation, with a focus on creating and sustaining valued roles for people with disabilities.
fieldData.name: Disability Work Management and Supported Employment

fieldData.course-description: Learn how websites are built from the ground up. This course introduces HTML, CSS, and JavaScript to help you create responsive, interactive web pages.
fieldData.extendededcoursedesc:
This course introduces HyperText Markup Language (HTML), Cascading Style Sheets (CSS), and JavaScript for building web page structure, styling, and interactivity. Students learn how browsers interpret HTML and how to create responsive, visually engaging pages using CSS. The course also explores JavaScript to develop interactive client-side functionality.

‍
fieldData.name: Web and Internet Fundamentals

fieldData.course-description: Build the core thinking skills behind software development. This course teaches you how to solve problems with structured programming, logical design, and clean, effective code.
fieldData.extendededcoursedesc: Computer programming is central to software development. In this course, students analyze basic software and technology problems while developing logical thinking and strong programming practices. They write structured, high-quality code using control flow, repetition, block structures, and subroutines to build effective solutions.
fieldData.name: Programming Fundamentals

fieldData.course-description: Explore how multiculturalism shapes Canada’s criminal justice system. This course examines diversity, Indigenous histories, and practical approaches to working effectively with communities across policing and corrections.
fieldData.extendededcoursedesc: This course examines multiculturalism and its relationship to the criminal justice system in Canada. Students explore ethnic, racial, religious, and cultural diversity within Canada’s multicultural framework, with an emphasis on Indigenous histories and traditions. The course also considers how these issues relate to policing, corrections, and other areas of the justice system, while building skills to work effectively with diverse communities.
fieldData.name: Diversity and Criminal Justice in Canada

fieldData.course-description: Follow how an individual moves through Canada’s criminal justice system from arrest to corrections. This course explores how police, courts, and corrections work together, and the decisions that shape each step.
fieldData.extendededcoursedesc: This course studies Canada’s criminal justice system from the perspective of an offender moving through it. Students examine the structure and jurisdictions of the three levels of government, as well as the roles of police, courts, and correctional agencies. Key topics include sentencing philosophies, correctional institutions, community corrections, diversion, discretion, limits of authority, and key decision points throughout the system.
fieldData.name: Introduction to the Criminal Justice System

fieldData.course-description: Build understanding of Fetal Alcohol Spectrum Disorder and its lifelong impacts. This course explores diagnosis, behaviour, ethics, and the supports available for individuals and families.
fieldData.extendededcoursedesc: Students examine the effects of prenatal alcohol exposure on individuals, families, communities, and broader systems. They explore ethical considerations, the diagnosis process for Fetal Alcohol Spectrum Disorder (FASD), and the complex behaviours associated with FASD. The course also focuses on identifying needs, prioritizing supports, and reviewing services available to individuals living with FASD and their families.
fieldData.name: Fetal Alcohol Spectrum Awareness  for Human Service Professionals

fieldData.course-description: Explore how play shapes learning and development in early childhood. This course brings together Indigenous perspectives, creativity, and hands-on design of play spaces that encourage curiosity and growth.
fieldData.extendededcoursedesc:
Through multiple worldviews, including Indigenous perspectives, students explore how play supports child development. The course examines how environments influence creativity and curiosity and applies evidence-based approaches to extend play through risk-taking, problem-solving, and inquiry. Students also design play spaces using natural materials and loose parts to support growth and engagement.

‍
fieldData.name: Developing Through Play

fieldData.course-description: Discover how early childhood education in Canada has evolved and what shapes today’s practice. This course explores policy, ethics, and inclusive approaches that support meaningful early learning experiences for young children.
fieldData.extendededcoursedesc: This course explores the historical roots of early childhood education in Canada, along with evolving pedagogical approaches and key societal shifts that have shaped the field. Students examine policies, regulations, professional standards, and ethical considerations that guide inclusive, developmentally appropriate early learning and child care. The course builds understanding of how these factors support positive learning experiences for young children.
fieldData.name: Introduction to Early Childhood Education and Development

fieldData.course-description: Learn how behaviour communicates needs and how to respond with supportive strategies. This course explores practical approaches to help individuals thrive across home, school, work, and community settings.
fieldData.extendededcoursedesc: This course introduces human behaviour as a form of communication. Students examine positive behavioural strategies to support individuals across home, school, work, and community settings.
fieldData.name: Positive Behaviour Support

fieldData.course-description: Explore how society shapes the way we understand death, dying, and grief. This course examines cultural, medical, and social perspectives while encouraging thoughtful reflection on one of life’s most universal experiences.
fieldData.extendededcoursedesc: This course explores death, dying, and bereavement through a sociological lens, examining how these experiences are shaped by social, cultural, and historical contexts. Students apply sociological theory to understand how dying is organized through legal, medical, familial, religious, and spiritual systems, and how meaning varies across cultures and time. The course also explores grief and bereavement through scholarly and creative works, encouraging reflection on the social forces that shape personal understandings of death.
fieldData.name: Sociology of Death and Dying

fieldData.course-description: Discover how social forces shape the way we think, feel, and act. This course explores identity, influence, prejudice, and relationships through real-world examples and interactive learning.
fieldData.extendededcoursedesc: This course examines how society influences thinking, feelings, and behaviour. Students explore key areas of social psychology, including social cognition, perception, identity, attitudes, influence, power, prejudice, stereotypes, groups, and relationships. Core theories and methods are applied to real-life contexts through discussions, reflections, and individual and group work.
fieldData.name: Social Psychology

fieldData.course-description: Explore the physics behind electricity, magnetism, and heat. This course covers circuits, fields, gases, and the fundamental laws that govern energy and matter.
fieldData.extendededcoursedesc:
This course introduces electricity, magnetism, and thermodynamics. Topics include electric and magnetic forces and fields, electric potential, circuits, pressure, ideal gases, and the first law of thermodynamics.

‍
fieldData.name: Modern Physics

fieldData.course-description: Explore the big questions behind right and wrong. This course introduces ethical theories and helps you think through how we judge actions, outcomes, and moral responsibility.
fieldData.extendededcoursedesc:
How do we decide what's right and wrong, or judge the outcomes of our actions? What makes an action worth doing, and what does it mean to make things go better?

In this introduction to ethics, we'll explore the tools we have for deciding what is good or bad, while comparing relevant theories and arguments that help us decide for ourselves. We will delve into the appraisal of human actions, of what is good and evil, right or wrong, and what it means to be morally responsible.
fieldData.name: Ethics

fieldData.course-description: Build the mathematical tools behind modern computing, engineering, and data science. This course explores matrices, vectors, and linear systems, along with key concepts like eigenvalues and transformations.
fieldData.extendededcoursedesc: This course introduces systems of linear equations, vectors in ℝⁿ, and matrix algebra. Additional topics include linear transformations, determinants, complex numbers, eigenvalues, and related applications.
fieldData.name: Linear Methods I

fieldData.course-description: Take calculus further and into multiple dimensions. This course covers advanced integration, series, and the foundations of multivariable calculus, including partial derivatives and multiple integrals.
fieldData.extendededcoursedesc: This course concludes single-variable calculus and introduces multivariable calculus. Topics include techniques of integration, sequences and series, convergence tests, and Taylor series, along with partial differentiation, multiple integration, parametric equations, and applications.
fieldData.name: Introductory Calculus II

fieldData.course-description: Take calculus further and into multiple dimensions. This course covers advanced integration, series, and the foundations of multivariable calculus, including partial derivatives and multiple integrals.
fieldData.extendededcoursedesc:
This course concludes single-variable calculus and introduces multivariable calculus. Topics include techniques of integration, sequences and series, convergence tests, and Taylor series, along with partial differentiation, multiple integration, parametric equations, and applications.

‍
fieldData.name: Introductory Calculus

fieldData.course-description: Learn how to make sense of data and turn it into insight. This course covers statistics, probability, and real-world applications across fields like health, business, and science.
fieldData.extendededcoursedesc:
This course introduces the basic principles of statistics and probability, along with hands-on use of statistical software and data collection methods. Students learn descriptive statistics to visualize and analyze data distributions, correlations, and regressions. The course also covers inferential statistics, including confidence intervals, hypothesis testing, and one-way ANOVA, with applications across fields such as science, business, health, education, law, politics, and sports.

‍
fieldData.name: Introduction to Statistics I

fieldData.course-description: Explore how films reflect and shape culture, identity, and society. This course introduces film analysis through powerful North American cinema focused on themes like race, gender, and history.
fieldData.extendededcoursedesc:
This course introduces the fundamentals of film studies, including key theories and methods of critical film analysis. Students examine English-language films from North America that explore themes such as gender, race, identity, and sociopolitical history. They apply film studies concepts and critical thinking skills to analyze different elements of film.

‍
fieldData.name: Topics in Film Genre

fieldData.course-description: Explore how children’s literature shapes identity, empathy, and understanding through stories, genres, and thoughtful book selection focused on growth.
fieldData.extendededcoursedesc:
This course introduces classic and contemporary children’s literature, providing an overview of its history and context. Students examine reading practices as shaped by social context and explore a range of genres and theories, including narrative therapy, with a focus on social justice and identity. The course also considers practical ways to support children in selecting books that foster empathy and self-understanding.

‍
fieldData.name: Children's Literature

fieldData.course-description: Explore how literature reflects culture, identity, and lived experience. This course engages with diverse voices, including Indigenous perspectives, through close reading and critical analysis.
fieldData.extendededcoursedesc:
Students explore how literature reflects and responds to social and cultural contexts, viewing it as a cultural practice shaped by the world around us. Through close reading and analysis, they engage with texts representing diverse perspectives, including Indigenous voices from what is now called Canada.

‍
fieldData.name: Literature and Society

fieldData.course-description: Build a strong foundation in university chemistry by exploring how reactions behave and interact. This course connects core concepts like kinetics, equilibrium, thermodynamics, and redox chemistry through real chemical systems.
fieldData.extendededcoursedesc:
This course introduces university-level chemistry from both theoretical and practical perspectives. Students explore key connections between kinetics, equilibria, and thermodynamics, along with acidity/basicity and redox behaviour using inorganic and organic examples.

‍
fieldData.name: General Chemistry: Change and Equilibrium

fieldData.course-description: Explore how DNA shapes life and drives evolution. This course examines inheritance, gene expression, natural selection, and the processes that create biodiversity.
fieldData.extendededcoursedesc:
This course examines the role of DNA in the inheritance of genetic information and identifies central concepts in evolution. Students explore principles of DNA replication and gene expression, as well as natural selection and speciation. Students further investigate how genetics and evolution contribute to biodiversity.

‍
fieldData.name: DNA, Inheritance, and Evolution

fieldData.course-description: Explore how gender shapes lived experience and social systems. This course introduces feminist theories, the history of women’s movements, and intersectional analysis of identity and inequality.
fieldData.extendededcoursedesc:
This interdisciplinary course provides an introduction to women’s and gender studies. It presents significant historical developments of the women’s movement, along with key feminist theoretical perspectives that explain and challenge the gendered nature of social relations. Through texts and social issues, students use an intersectional approach to critically analyze women’s lives across diverse social locations, including race/ethnicity, religion, class, age, sexuality, and ability.

‍
fieldData.name: Introduction to Women and Gender Studies

fieldData.course-description: Aging, while an individual experience, is also an experience that is heavily influenced by social structures and social processes. Using the sociological perspective, this course explores contemporary aging by examining choices and experiences that transcend the individual and incorporate larger social groups and processes. In doing so, learners build a foundation in sociological concepts and theories to apply this knowledge to age-related issues. Learners consider demographic factors leading to population aging; the role of social structures and processes in shaping experiences of physical aging; as well as aging in relation to health systems, retirement, social engagement, and family in Canadian society.
fieldData.extendededcoursedesc: Sociology of Aging
fieldData.name: Sociology of Aging

fieldData.course-description: In this course, learners explore how families are integrated within larger social systems; how patterns of social power and inequality shape Canadian families; as well as how and why the family is critical to the socialization process. The course culminates in the critical assessment of issues affecting families in Canada.
fieldData.extendededcoursedesc: Sociology of the Family
fieldData.name: Sociology of the Family

fieldData.course-description: This course provides an introductory overview of the discipline of Sociology. Learners explore human behaviour, stratification, social institutions, and sociological theory and methods. Learners examine how social positions shape lives, and how people adjust to social and cultural environments.
fieldData.extendededcoursedesc: Introduction to Sociology
fieldData.name: Introduction to Sociology

fieldData.course-description: This introductory course provides learners with a basic understanding and overview of the field of psychology. Attention is given to major psychological perspectives and the fundamentals of scientific thinking, biological factors, cognitive processes, social and cultural influences, personality, psychological disorders, and human motivation. Learners are encouraged to apply what they learn to their own lives and the world around them.
fieldData.extendededcoursedesc: Introduction To Psychology
fieldData.name: Introduction To Psychology

fieldData.course-description: This course provides a comprehensive overview of human growth and development and typical behavioural responses throughout the life span. You will analyze human development across four domains: physical, cognitive, social, and emotional. Emphasis is placed upon the stages of development and their linkage to common events occurring during these stages.
fieldData.extendededcoursedesc: Human Growth And Development Across The Life Span
fieldData.name: Human Growth And Development Across The Life Span

fieldData.course-description: This course provides an introduction to the diverse Indigenous Nations of Canada, while looking at the effects of colonialism in both historical and contemporary times, and from multiple perspectives. This course will orient learners to the current goals and challenges of Indigenous communities in Canada today. Learners are encouraged to situate themselves in Truth and Reconciliation and the Calls to Action, especially as they relate to their chosen field of work.
fieldData.extendededcoursedesc: Introduction to Indigenous Studies
fieldData.name: Introduction to Indigenous Studies

fieldData.course-description: This first-year composition course introduces learners to academic writing and critical thinking. They read and analyze sociopolitical, cultural, and gender issues in texts with an emphasis on the experiences of people whose voices were historically silenced, particularly those of Indigenous communities in Canada. Learners develop strategies to communicate their own ideas and integrate them with those of others by quoting, paraphrasing, and summarizing source material. Learners present their written assignments professionally according to APA formatting guidelines.
fieldData.extendededcoursedesc: English Composition
fieldData.name: English Composition

fieldData.course-description: This course examines parametric and simulation-based hypothesis testing and associated errors. Students use confidence intervals and hypothesis testing for differences between two parameters, both parametric and simulation-based. The course also incorporates tests of association and goodness-of-fit, along with statistical modeling and parametric testing of both the simple and multiple models. Students perform diagnostic checking and analysis of variance.
fieldData.extendededcoursedesc: Introduction to Statistics II
fieldData.name: Introduction to Statistics II

fieldData.course-description: Students will learn the basic principles of statistics, acquire the skills to solve elementary statistical and probability problems, and gain hands-on experience with well-known statistical software, as well as basic methods for collecting data. Students will also learn the main tools of descriptive statistics to visualize collected data, analyze data distributions, and establish correlations and regressions between random variables. The course will also cover the main tools of inferential statistics for estimating mean values and proportions by confidence intervals, hypotheses testing, and one-way ANOVA. Applications are taken from wide range of subject areas such as biology and environmental science, business and economics, health sciences, education, crime and law, politics, social studies, and sports and entertainment.
fieldData.extendededcoursedesc: Statistics I
fieldData.name: Statistics I

fieldData.course-description: This course introduces the basic concepts of transportation and warehousing operations. Learners explore the dynamic flow and storage of materials, services, and related information from suppliers to the final customers. In this course, learners examine the theories and best practices in logistics that lead companies to achieve efficient and effective operations to serve their customers and overcome their competitors.
fieldData.extendededcoursedesc: Logistics & Transportation
fieldData.name: Logistics & Transportation

fieldData.course-description: Negotiation skills are an essential competency for any manager, especially for those in supply chain management. This course provides learners with a roadmap for leading or participating in successful negotiations. Students will focus on the negotiation process, and learn the activities and techniques to be used from the preparation stage to the actual face-to-face negotiations. The course covers understanding the other negotiator, responding to power imbalances, as well as looking beyond the deal to build longer-term relationships. Interactive activities, including negotiation simulations and role-playing exercises, feature prominently and allow for opportunities to fine-tune the student's negotiation skills.
fieldData.extendededcoursedesc: Negotiation Skills
fieldData.name: Negotiation Skills

fieldData.course-description: The design and management of products, processes, services, and supply chains is accomplished by an organization�s operations management function. This course examines the integration of critical business processes from planning to short-term scheduling. Topics include operations planning and productivity, capacity and strategy design, process and product design using industry standards, facility layout and location models, job and staff scheduling, and queuing theory.
fieldData.extendededcoursedesc: Operations Management I
fieldData.name: Operations Management I

fieldData.course-description: Supply chain management (SCM) is the movement of material and information through integrated processes in a supply chain to provide the highest degree of customer satisfaction at the lowest possible cost to achieve a sustainable competitive advantage. The key building blocks of a supply chain, logistics, procurement, and operations execution, will be covered. Learners will explore the scope of SCM and its impact on organizations.
fieldData.extendededcoursedesc: Introduction to Supply Chain Management
fieldData.name: Introduction to Supply Chain Management

fieldData.course-description: Learners are introduced to concepts aimed at providing a solid foundation of marketing principles and the role marketing plays in business. Emphasizing a holistic approach, learners have the opportunity to analyze and apply the marketing mix. Key concepts include product, price, placement, and promotion (4Ps), the Integrated Marketing Communications Mix (IMC), market research, and consumer behaviour.
fieldData.extendededcoursedesc: Introduction to Marketing
fieldData.name: Introduction to Marketing

fieldData.course-description: This course introduces statistics for business disciplines. The course begins with an introduction to descriptive statistics and probability theory, then builds to a thorough understanding of theories and methods used in model building, estimation, and interpretation. Emphasis is placed on applying real data, technology, and statistical data analysis techniques to business problems to promote critical and informed business decisions and conclusions.
fieldData.extendededcoursedesc: Introductory Statistics for Business Disciplines
fieldData.name: Introductory Statistics for Business Disciplines

fieldData.course-description: Learners critically evaluate day-to-day economic subjects in a personal and business context. Throughout the course the economy is examined at the aggregate level with an emphasis on the determination and measurement of national income in the short and long run. The role of households, businesses, government, financial intermediaries and the international sector in influencing national income is examined. Learners analyze business cycles, money and banking, inflation, unemployment, exchange rates, and fiscal and monetary policies.
fieldData.extendededcoursedesc: Macroeconomics
fieldData.name: Macroeconomics

fieldData.course-description: This course provides hands-on learning with Microsoft Excel and its applications in today�s business environment. Learners develop skills to navigate, consolidate, and analyze data across multiple worksheets. Learners also create macros for efficient analysis, manage complex nested formulas for scenario planning, and design effective corporate dashboards.
fieldData.extendededcoursedesc: Microsoft Excel
fieldData.name: Microsoft Excel

fieldData.course-description: A basic understanding of key elements of the law is an essential factor in successful business management. Learners apply legal fundamentals useful in today�s fast- paced, rapidly changing business environment.
fieldData.extendededcoursedesc: Business Law
fieldData.name: Business Law

fieldData.course-description: This course will cover business uses of math and algebra with specific topics including: percentages; ratios, proportions and currency exchange; merchandise mathematics; break-even and cost-volume-profit analysis; simple interest; compound interest including present and future value, annuities, loans and mortgages.
fieldData.extendededcoursedesc: Business Mathematics
fieldData.name: Business Mathematics

fieldData.course-description: Both microeconomics and macroeconomics are crucial for shaping business decisions and strategies across various organizational levels. Accountants and supply chain management professionals must possess a foundational understanding of economics, as it profoundly impacts business operations. This course introduces microeconomics and macroeconomics, providing essential knowledge for informed decision-making in consumer choices, entrepreneurship, investments, and informed citizens evaluating government policies. Microeconomics examines cost-benefit analysis in decision-making, covering topics like trade advantages, price coordination, competition, efficiency-equity trade-offs, government interventions, environmental policies, and income distribution. In contrast, macroeconomics assesses the overall performance of market economies, including GDP, economic growth, business cycles, unemployment, inflation, monetary policies, exchange rates, government deficits, globalization, and trade policies.
fieldData.extendededcoursedesc: Principles of Economics
fieldData.name: Principles of Economics

fieldData.course-description: This course is aimed at providing a hands-on learning experience with a Windows operating system and computer applications (Microsoft Office: Word, Excel, Outlook, and PowerPoint) used in a business environment. Learners will develop skills and gain experience to create business documents, navigate, consolidate, and analyze data across multiple worksheets, manage professional communications, and create electronic presentations.
fieldData.extendededcoursedesc: Computer Applications
fieldData.name: Computer Applications

fieldData.course-description: Introduction to organizations and sustainability articulates a management approach to integrating economic, ethical, and environmental responsibilities into all aspects of organizations working to benefit society. Learners examine ethics of business and constructs of morally appropriate behavior concerning decision-making and businesses' relationship with the community. Concepts and practical approaches are used to discuss and integrate sustainability criteria with business requirements, including performance management and evolving strategies as business needs change.
fieldData.extendededcoursedesc: Introduction to Organizations and Sustainability
fieldData.name: Introduction to Organizations and Sustainability

fieldData.course-description: With today's dynamic business climate and diverse workforce, the demands of managers to engage employees, be innovative, and be adaptive have become paramount to organizational effectiveness. As a result, managers are required to demonstrate a diverse range of skills which include, but are not limited to: planning and strategic management; effective decision-making and critical thinking; organizing human capital to facilitate efficient and effective work-practices; fostering positive influence to engage a diverse workforce with a focus on employee wellbeing, satisfaction, and performance; and implementing controls to establish and measure performance. This course provides the opportunity for students to explore key management concepts and the multi-faceted role of a manager within an organization.
fieldData.extendededcoursedesc: Introduction to Management
fieldData.name: Introduction to Management

fieldData.course-description: Litigation is the process by which private disputes are resolved within the Alberta court system. This course examines the court structure and how to reference the Alberta Rules of Court. Learners explore how plaintiffs bring claims to court and how defendants can defend against those claims. Introductory steps in a civil litigation dispute are covered up to a process called �Questioning.� Knowledge is applied by preparing key documents used in the civil litigation process.

fieldData.name: Introduction to the Legal Profession

fieldData.course-description: In this course learners are introduced to Canadian health care system structure, legislation, and information systems. Learners explore how the principles of safety, confidentiality, privacy, and security apply to the health care setting.

fieldData.name: Introduction to Health Care Fundamentals

fieldData.course-description: Learners examine interdisciplinary roles and responsibilities needed to be successful in an administrative support role within healthcare. fieldData.course-description: The central theme of the course focuses on the relationship between thinking, human behaviour, and organizational effectiveness. Opportunity is provided for learners to experience incidental learning as they evaluate their own behaviour. Learners explore how concepts and ideas pertaining to human behaviour can transform self, relationships, and the workplace.
fieldData.extendededcoursedesc: Organizational Behaviour
fieldData.name: Organizational Behaviour

This course deeply explores how to finance an organization�s identified risks within the existing financial marketplace. Various finance strategies will be examined, such as self-insurance, insurance, reinsurance, captive insurers, and capital markets. Learners are introduced to contractual risk transfer strategies and how to allocate costs associated with hazard risks as well.
fieldData.extendededcoursedesc: Risk Financing
fieldData.name: Risk Financing

fieldData.course-description: Risk management is critical for an organization�s operation. The ability to identify, assess, manage, and monitor risks benefits a business�s sustainability and continuity in today�s evolving society. This course introduces the fundamental principles and concepts of risk management. Learners practice and apply the risk management standards, framework, process, and strategies through the course.

fieldData.name: Risk Management Principles and Practice

fieldData.course-description: Risk impacts our daily lives. Through the examination of insurance and risk management, learners explore risk control techniques, laws, concepts, and practices commonly encountered in the insurance industry.
fieldData.extendededcoursedesc: Introduction to Insurance and Risk Management
fieldData.name: Introduction to Insurance and Risk Management

fieldData.course-description: In this course, students will have their first look at esports from an entry-level perspective. This course will introduce topics such as the history of esports, the difference between gaming and esports, esports culture, and touch on some topics that will be taught throughout the rest of the esports business management diploma program.

fieldData.name: Introduction to Esports

fieldData.course-description: This course explores the concepts and key fundamentals of managerial accounting used for planning, controlling, and measuring operations. Focus is on short-term management decision-making and the techniques, methods, and systems of performance reporting and evaluation used to assist management. Learners explore a variety of costing systems, cost-volume-profit relationships, budgeting, and variance analysis, which are essential to understanding business operations.

fieldData.course-description: Websites and website design are important in the field of digital marketing. This course introduces the principles of website design and focuses on usability and design aesthetics. Learners explore trends in web publication and incorporate design considerations like iconography, work-flow, graphics, menus, and layout into the production of websites that address business needs.
fieldData.extendededcoursedesc: Introduction to Web Design for Digital Marketing
fieldData.name: Introduction to Web Design for Digital Marketing

fieldData.course-description: Effective keyboarding is an integral part of being successful in an office environment. Focus is placed on ergonomic touch-typing technique to master the alphabetic and numeric keyboard. Learners with keyboarding experience have the opportunity to improve their technique to achieve higher level of speed and accuracy.
fieldData.extendededcoursedesc: Introduction to Professional Keyboarding
fieldData.name: Introduction to Professional Keyboarding

This course covers key tools, filters, and layers in the creation and manipulation of images, building foundational skills in the use of creative production software. A combination of photography, typography, drawing, computer graphics, brainstorming techniques, and production methods are addressed, as well as interactive design. Learners explore techniques combining photographic and illustrative material using imaging software to produce digital based visuals, collages, and conceptual mock-ups with both bitmap and vector elements.
fieldData.extendededcoursedesc: Introduction to Digital Media Production
fieldData.name: Introduction to Digital Media Production

fieldData.extendededcoursedesc: Learners critically evaluate day-to-day economic subjects in a personal and business context. Throughout the course the economy is examined at the aggregate level with an emphasis on the determination and measurement of national income in the short and long run. The role of households, businesses, government, financial intermediaries and the international sector in influencing national income is examined. Learners analyze business cycles, money and banking, inflation, unemployment, exchange rates, and fiscal and monetary policies.
fieldData.name: Macroeconomics

fieldData.extendededcoursedesc:
Employment Law plays a critical role in human resources management. This course equips learners with the knowledge and skills to apply employment and common law to the workplace. By using employment scenarios, learners strategize how they could help employers reduce risk and resolve human resource issues. The importance of ethical human resource policies and procedures and ways to address the emerging risks of the digital workplace will also be explored.

‍
fieldData.name: Employment Law

fieldData.extendededcoursedesc: This course examines parametric and simulation-based hypothesis testing and associated errors. Students use confidence intervals and hypothesis testing for differences between two parameters, both parametric and simulation-based. The course also incorporates tests of association and goodness-of-fit, along with statistical modeling and parametric testing of both the simple and multiple models. Students perform diagnostic checking and analysis of variance.
fieldData.name: Introduction to Statistics II

fieldData.extendededcoursedesc:
Students will learn the basic principles of statistics, acquire the skills to solve elementary statistical and probability problems, and gain hands-on experience with well-known statistical software, as well as basic methods for collecting data. Students will also learn the main tools of descriptive statistics to visualize collected data, analyze data distributions, and establish correlations and regressions between random variables. The course will also cover the main tools of inferential statistics for estimating mean values and proportions by confidence intervals, hypotheses testing, and one-way ANOVA. Applications are taken from wide range of subject areas such as biology and environmental science, business and economics, health sciences, education, crime and law, politics, social studies, and sports and entertainment.

‍
fieldData.name: Statistics I

The course begins with an introduction to descriptive statistics and probability theory, then builds to a thorough understanding of theories and methods used in model building, estimation, and interpretation. Emphasis is placed on applying real data, technology, and statistical data analysis techniques to business problems to promote critical and informed business decisions and conclusions.
fieldData.name: Introductory Statistics for Business Disciplines

fieldData.extendededcoursedesc: This course explores strategic, ethical, and technological dimensions of talent acquisition in the Canadian context. Students design and implement talent acquisition and retention processes that align with organizational strategy while leveraging workforce planning, AI, and people analytics. Emphasis will be placed on enhancing candidate experience, optimizing Employee Value Proposition EVP, and fostering inclusion and diversity. Students will evaluate the legal frameworks governing HR practices, examine the role of data and innovation in recruitment, and develop skills to support workforce mobility, retention, and collaboration in a rapidly evolving, digital-driven environment.
fieldData.name: Talent Acquisition and Retention

fieldData.extendededcoursedesc: This course examines the principles of colour theory and its relationship with interior space, light, and materials. Learners apply this knowledge in their consultation with a client, to create and present a lighting plan that addresses spacial requirements and client need.
fieldData.name: Colour and Light in Decorating

fieldData.extendededcoursedesc: Negotiation skills are an essential competency for any manager, especially for those in supply chain management. This course provides learners with a roadmap for leading or participating in successful negotiations. Students will focus on the negotiation process, and learn the activities and techniques to be used from the preparation stage to the actual face-to-face negotiations. The course covers understanding the other negotiator, responding to power imbalances, as well as looking beyond the deal to build longer-term relationships. Interactive activities, including negotiation simulations and role-playing exercises, feature prominently and allow for opportunities to fine-tune the students negotiation skills.
fieldData.name: Negotiation Skills

fieldData.extendededcoursedesc: This course provides an interdisciplinary overview of Canada’s past, present, and future. Emphasizing critical thinking skills, it introduces students to concepts and tools for understanding this country’s multifaceted regional and national identities from diverse social, cultural, political, economic, and ethnic perspectives.
fieldData.name: Introduction to Canadian Studies

fieldData.extendededcoursedesc: Learners use HyperText Markup Language HTML, Cascading Style Sheets CSS, and JavaScript a mix of programming and layout that powers the visuals and interactions on the web in this course. They also use the elements of a web page and describe how the HTML code is interpreted by a web browser to display the pages visual components. They are able to style a wide range of design elements and enhance the visual components. Further, they apply CSS properties to create completely responsive and aesthetically pleasing web pages. Learners explore the dynamics of JavaScript, the webs most popular, extensively used, and incredibly powerful language as well to develop interactive client-side functionality.
fieldData.name: Web and Internet Fundamentals

fieldData.extendededcoursedesc: Computer programming is central to software development. Learners analyze basic software and technology problems and develop a good programming style and logical thinking to write structured instruction that addresses those problems. Learners demonstrate their structured coding skills by writing correct code with clarity and quality. They use extensively the structured control flow, repetition, block structure, and subroutines in this course.
fieldData.name: Programming Fundamentals

fieldData.extendededcoursedesc: This course introduces the basic concepts of transportation and warehousing operations. Learners explore the dynamic flow and storage of materials, services, and related information from suppliers to the final customers. In this course, learners examine the theories and best practices in logistics that lead companies to achieve efficient and effective operations to serve their customers and overcome their competitors.
fieldData.name: Logistics & Transportation

fieldData.extendededcoursedesc: Operations management is the administration of all activities that transform inputs to outputs for all goods and services. This course explores the design and management of products, processes, services, and supply chains. Learners examine the integration of critical business processes from planning to short-term scheduling.
fieldData.name: Operations Management I

fieldData.extendededcoursedesc: This course explores the development of Canadian political institutions and political issues in Canada. Learners explore contemporary Canadian politics by examining concepts such as the evolution of federalism, the Constitution, parliament, elections, Indigenous and minority rights, and multiculturalism. Learners will apply political science terms and concepts to the analysis of contemporary Canadian political issues.
fieldData.name: Canadian Politics: Institutions and Issues

fieldData.extendededcoursedesc: This course is an introduction to classical mechanics. Topics include motion in one and two dimensions, Newtons laws of motion, torque, rotations, conservation of energy, and conservation of momentum. Concepts are further explored during hands-on labs.
fieldData.name: Mechanics

fieldData.extendededcoursedesc: Both microeconomics and macroeconomics are crucial for shaping business decisions and strategies across various organizational levels. Accountants and supply chain management professionals must possess a foundational understanding of economics, as it profoundly impacts business operations. This course introduces microeconomics and macroeconomics, providing essential knowledge for informed decision-making in consumer choices, entrepreneurship, investments, and informed citizens evaluating government policies. Microeconomics examines cost-benefit analysis in decision-making, covering topics like trade advantages, price coordination, competition, efficiency-equity trade-offs, government interventions, environmental policies, and income distribution. In contrast, macroeconomics assesses the overall performance of market economies, including GDP, economic growth, business cycles, unemployment, inflation, monetary policies, exchange rates, government deficits, globalization, and trade policies.
fieldData.name: Principles of Economics

fieldData.extendededcoursedesc: This course examines the fundamental concepts of differential and integral calculus, and how to apply these concepts to solve practical problems. Learners gain a theoretical understanding of calculus by working with functions of one variable and apply fundamental concepts to solve problems in related rates, optimization of functions, and mathematical modeling. Learners use these techniques to solve applied problems in business, economics, natural sciences, and engineering.
fieldData.name: Introductory Calculus

Learners apply the principles and elements of design in the creation of client profiles and decorating solutions addressing the requirements of an interior space and client need.
fieldData.name: Principles & Elements of Design

fieldData.extendededcoursedesc: Learners apply their knowledge of human resource functions through multiple stakeholder lenses while aligning functions to an organization’s vision and strategy. Utilizing business scenarios, learners transition through the employment cycle adhering to legal requirements, ensuring health and safety in the workplace, and building positive work culture initiatives.
fieldData.name: Introduction to Human Resources

fieldData.extendededcoursedesc: This course explores the role of a health and human services manager when working alongside or within the structure of the Canadian health system. The roles and responsibilities of the different levels of government, including the importance of legislation such as the Canada Health Act, regulations, and guidelines are discussed. Through an analysis of contemporary issues the strengths, limitations, and potential gaps in services in the Canadian universal health system are explored.
fieldData.name: Managing and the Canadian Health System

fieldData.extendededcoursedesc: In the spirit of reconciliation, learners explore Truth and Reconciliation Calls to Action TRC 2015 through sharing circles, storytelling, art, language and culture, and traditional knowledge, while examining the impact of colonization and legacy of residential schools. As future leaders in health and human services, learners focus on implementing Calls to Action that apply to the sector while investigating organizational and systems changes that contribute to the ongoing process of decolonization and reconciliation.
fieldData.name: Implementing TRC (2015) Calls to Action in Health and Human Services

fieldData.extendededcoursedesc: This course examines the concepts of common chronic illness while focusing on managing chronic conditions and maintaining quality of life. Learners apply the current evidence-informed principles in chronic illness prevention and management, program facilitation, and program evaluation.
fieldData.name: Chronic Illness Management

fieldData.extendededcoursedesc: This course will assess the methods which an organization can obtain funds to pay for accidental losses. Emphasis is placed on the selection, implementation and monitoring of various risk financing techniques. Specific subjects discussed are: a framework for risk financing criteria for risk financing selection techniques insurance as a mechanism for financing property, net income, personnel, and liability losses accounting and income tax aspects of accidental losses insurance pricing selection of insurers and their representatives implementing risk retention available options, including the use of affiliated insurers and cost of risk allocation techniques.
fieldData.name: Risk Financing

fieldData.extendededcoursedesc: The purpose of this course is to develop an enterprise-wide perspective of risk by applying risk management concepts to four major categories: hazard insurable, operational, financial, and strategic. This course broadens your understanding of risk management from its traditional focus on accidental losses to include all risks an organization may face. Learn about global risk management standards such as ISO 31000 and the COSO ERM Integrated Framework, and discuss various risk identification and analysis techniques in detail. Apply rudimentary analytical tools to assess financial risk in areas of financial leverage, liquidity risk, and capital investment risk. Risk oversight, monitoring, and assurance are discussed from the perspective of governance and internal control. This course relies heavily on insurance based content consistent with risk assessment and risk management principles.
fieldData.name: Risk Assessment and Treatment

fieldData.extendededcoursedesc: This second-year course explores crime in various storytelling forms, such as literature, film, and television. Analyzing detective fiction, true crime, film noir, and more, learners consider how stories about crime reflect and challenge societal views on law, morality, and justice. Learners examine elements of crime narrative, such as plot, character, and theme, while enriching their understanding of the historical contexts and ethical dimensions of crime narratives. Learners critique and research crime narratives, developing evidence-based arguments in written assignments and class discussions.
fieldData.name: Crime Narrative

fieldData.extendededcoursedesc: Learners explore the relationship of literature to the world around us, considering how literature is a cultural practice that responds to and reflects its social context. Learners engage in close reading and analysis of texts that reflect diverse perspectives, including those Indigenous to what is now called Canada.
fieldData.name: Literature and Society

fieldData.extendededcoursedesc: This course develops knowledge of the history, philosophy, legislation, values, trends and issues related to exceptional learners. It explores student inclusion and provides a wide overview of exceptionalities ranging from mild to severe and child to adulthood. Access and retrieval of information on exceptionalities is emphasized.
fieldData.name: Introduction to Exceptionalities

fieldData.extendededcoursedesc: This course introduces the principles of design through exercises, projects, rapid ideation and presentations. Learners will explore the principles of design, with a focus on process and composition across a variety of media and design software.
fieldData.name: Fundamental Principles of Digital Design

fieldData.extendededcoursedesc: Planning involves being able to envision a positive and valued future for and with the person and their network of allies. This course evaluates current planning strategies with emphasis on the philosophical principles and values inherent in those strategies. Learners practice writing clear implementation plans incorporating elements of inclusion, empowerment, and individualization.
fieldData.name: Person Centered Planning

fieldData.extendededcoursedesc: Disability Studies is a study of the social, cultural, historical, and philosophical perspectives of disability. It is grounded by the belief that the creation of knowledge about disability should be WITH/BY disabled people themselves. This course will provide learners with the historical background of disability and the contexts and paradigms it currently uses today. This course requires a C to be considered a pass.
fieldData.name: Introduction to Disability Studies

fieldData.extendededcoursedesc: This course focuses on the knowledge, attitudes, skills, and behaviours for appropriate and effective intercultural communication in diverse workplaces. Learners explore the importance of a global and ethnorelative perspective linking the concepts to their lived experiences. Areas of focus include cultural influences on communication, conflict styles, self-awareness, acculturation, and Indigenous worldviews.
fieldData.name: Intercultural Communication

fieldData.course-description: Understand how atoms come together to form the world around you. This course explores electronic structure, chemical bonding, and molecular interactions through real inorganic and organic examples.
fieldData.extendededcoursedesc: An introduction to university chemistry from theoretical and practical perspectives, that focuses on an exploration of the fundamental links between electronic structure, chemical bonding, molecular structure and the interactions of molecules using inorganic and organic examples.
fieldData.name: General Chemistry: Structure and Bonding

fieldData.course-description: Explore how living systems capture, use, and transfer energy across molecules, organisms, and ecosystems. This course connects metabolism, molecular structure, and ecological interactions to explain how life is powered.
fieldData.extendededcoursedesc: In this introductory course on bioenergetics, learners explore the use and transfer of energy in the plant and animal kingdoms from molecules to ecosystems and investigate how molecular structure determines biological function. They explore how energy is generated from metabolic reaction pathways as well as organisms’ interactions with the physical and biotic components of earth.
fieldData.name: Fundamentals of Bioenergetics

fieldData.extendededcoursedesc: This course introduces learners to foundational biological concepts and mechanisms. Learners explore the organization and processes of life at the cellular, organismal, species, and ecosystem levels. These concepts are illustrated through current examples of medical and environmental issues and discoveries.
fieldData.name: The Organization and Diversity of Life

fieldData.extendededcoursedesc: In this course, learners apply marketing principles using various digital analytic platforms to address data-driven organizational contexts. Learners analyze sample data sets to draw correlations between consumer behaviour, media, and campaign strategies as the basis for the formal presentation of performance and metrics. These activities lead to the evaluation of types of engagement through the customer lifecycle and how those engagements evolve to address changing consumer behaviour.

fieldData.extendededcoursedesc: This course provides an overview of the typical physical, social, emotional, moral, and cognitive developmental changes occurring during middle childhood and adolescence. Learners explore major theoretical concepts and strategies of interaction with individuals in this age group. Course activity focuses on typical and atypical aspects of development; the contexts and social spheres that shape middle childhood and adolescence; as well as transitions from middle childhood to adolescence.

fieldData.course-description: This course provides a comprehensive overview of human growth and development and typical behavioural responses throughout the lifespan.
fieldData.extendededcoursedesc: This course provides a comprehensive overview of human growth and development and typical behavioural responses throughout the lifespan. You will analyze human development across four domains: physical, cognitive, social, and emotional. Emphasis is placed upon the stages of development and their linkage to common events occurring during these stages.
fieldData.name: Human Growth and Development Across The Life Span

fieldData.course-description: This introductory course provides learners with a basic understanding and an overview of the field of psychology.
fieldData.extendededcoursedesc: This introductory course provides learners with a basic understanding and an overview of the field of psychology. Attention is given to major psychological perspectives and the fundamentals of scientific thinking, biological factors, sensation and perception, cognitive processes, personality, social influences and human motivation. Learners will be encouraged to apply what they learn to their own lives and the world around them.
fieldData.name: Introduction to Psychology

fieldData.extendededcoursedesc: Learners examine interdisciplinary roles and responsibilities needed to be successful in an administrative support role within healthcare. fieldData.course-description: This course focuses on the theories, practical skills, and broader issues to guide work in the field of addictions.
fieldData.extendededcoursedesc: This course focuses on the theories, practical skills, and broader issues to guide work in the field of addictions. Learners reflect on their beliefs and values to develop a professional practice drawing upon and respects the richness and depth of Canada's multicultural society and special populations. Learners explore the types of addictions, the breadth of addiction treatment theory, and how theory informs addiction treatment practice.
fieldData.name: Introduction to Addiction Studies
